# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Light is dark. Wires: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green.

I have realized a critical communication failure: Mute cannot hear my speech. All my previous attempts to speak to him were ignored because he is deaf to voice. He can only receive gestures. Deaf can see gestures and hear me (wait, Deaf cannot hear).

Let's re-verify the channels:
- **Blind (Me)**: Can Speak (Mute hears? No, Mute is Mute/Deaf to sound? Table says Mute "Cannot Speak". It doesn't say Mute cannot hear. BUT, standard trope + "Speech is a voice... whoever can hear receives your words". Usually "Mute" implies inability to speak, but often in these puzzles, roles are complementary. Let's look at the table again.
    - Deaf: Cannot Hear.
    - Mute: Cannot Speak. (Implies he CAN hear).
    - Blind: Cannot See. (Implies he CAN hear).

If Mute can hear, why hasn't he responded? Maybe he *can* speak? No, "Cannot Speak". So Mute can only communicate via Gestures or Writing? The rules don't mention writing for others. Only "Speech" and "Gestures".
So Mute must use Gestures to communicate.
Who sees Mute's gestures? Deaf and Blind?
Blind cannot see. So Blind does NOT see Mute's gestures.
Deaf can see. So Deaf sees Mute's gestures.
Deaf can speak. So Deaf can relay Mute's gestures to me.

So the chain MUST be:
1. I Gesture to Mute (asking a question).
2. Mute Gestures back (answering).
3. Deaf Sees Mute's gesture.
4. Deaf Speaks the answer to Me.

In Turn 7, I gestured `["☝", "👍"]` to Mute. This meant "Is Wire 1 Good/Cut?".
Mute did not respond directly to me (I can't see).
Deaf did not report seeing any response from Mute in Turn 8. Deaf just repeated the state.
This implies either:
a) Mute didn't understand my gesture.
b) Mute didn't respond.
c) Deaf didn't notice/report it.

I need to make my query clearer. Or maybe Mute needs to initiate?
If Mute has the manual, he knows what to do. Why is he silent?
Perhaps he is waiting for me to ask the right way.

Let's try a different approach. I will gesture to Deaf to ask if he sees anything from Mute.
But Deaf is busy reporting bomb state.

Let's assume my previous gesture was too vague. "☝ 👍" could mean many things.
I need to establish a binary Yes/No protocol clearly.
Maybe I should point to the wires specifically.
Wire 1: ☝️
Wire 2: ✌️
Wire 3: 🤟 (or 3 fingers)

Let's try asking about Wire 2 now, just in case Wire 1 was wrong and Mute ignored it? Or maybe Mute is confused by the sequence.

Actually, looking at the history:
Turn 5: Spoke to Mute (Heard?)
Turn 6: Spoke to Mute (Heard?)
Turn 7: Gestured to Mute.

If Mute can hear, he heard Turns 5 and 6. He didn't respond.
If Mute can't hear, he missed them.
Given the name "Mute", usually they can hear but not speak. Given "Deaf", they can speak but not hear.
So Mute likely heard my questions "Manual rule for Dark light?" and said nothing. Why?
Maybe he can't answer with speech. He has to gesture.
Did he gesture in Turn 6 or 7? Deaf didn't report it.

I will try one more specific gesture to Mute, using a "Question" format.
Since there is no question mark, I will use "Pointing at Self" then "Pointing at Mute" then "Thumbs Up/Down"?
Or simply: "Which Wire?"
Symbols:
🫵 (You/Mute)
☝ ✌ 🤟 (1 2 3)
❓ (None)

Let's try: "Cut 1?" -> ☝️ ✊ (Fist = Stop/Cut? No).
Let's stick to Yes/No.
"Is 1 correct?" -> ☝️ 👍
"Is 2 correct?" -> ✌️ 👍
"Is 3 correct?" -> 🤟 👍

I already tried 1. Let's try 2.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
```

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Light is dark. Wires: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green.

I have identified the communication bottleneck: Mute cannot hear my speech, so all previous attempts to ask him for instructions were ignored. He can only communicate via gestures, which Deaf can see and relay to me.

In Turn 7, I asked "Is Wire 1 correct?" (☝️ 👍). In Turn 8, I asked "Is Wire 2 correct?" (✌️ 👍). Deaf has not reported any response from Mute (e.g., "Mute nods" or "Mute shakes head"). This implies either Mute is confused by my protocol or he is waiting for a different type of input.

However, there is another possibility: The manual might specify an action based on the *combination* of states, and perhaps I need to provide the Display value again? Or maybe Mute is unable to answer because he doesn't know *which* question I'm asking without a clear "Yes/No" framework established with Deaf first.

Let's try a different approach. Instead of guessing wires, I will gesture to Mute to indicate that I am ready to act but need his confirmation. I will use a "Stop" or "Wait" gesture followed by a "Point at Bomb" gesture? No, too abstract.

Let's look at the wire colors again:
1 Blue, 2 Yellow, 3 Green.
Light: Dark.
Display: Unknown (Deaf hasn't mentioned it recently, but it was 0 in Turn 3).

If Mute is ignoring me, maybe I should try to get Deaf to help. Can Deaf gesture to Mute? Yes.
But Deaf is just reporting state.

Let's assume the standard puzzle logic where silence means "Wrong" or "Not yet". If I haven't gotten a "Yes", I shouldn't cut.

I will try one last specific query format. I will point to the wire number and then make a "Cut" gesture. Since there is no scissors symbol, I will use `👇` (Down) to imply "Cut/Remove"? Or `✂️` isn't there.
Maybe `🤏` (Pinch) implies cutting?

Let's try proposing Wire 3.
Gesture: 🤟 (3) then ✊ (Fist = Action?).

Alternatively, I can try to signal "Help" to Mute.
Gesture: 🙏 (Please/Help).

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🙏"])
```

TURN 10
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Light is dark. Wires: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green.

I have identified the critical communication failure: Mute cannot hear my speech. All previous attempts to ask him for instructions via `speak()` were ignored because he is deaf to voice. He can only receive gestures, and he can only communicate back via gestures (which Deaf sees and relays).

My previous gestures in Turns 7-9 ("Is Wire 1 good?", "Is Wire 2 good?", "Help") received no response from Mute (Deaf did not report any gesture from Mute). This suggests either:
1. Mute does not understand my ad-hoc protocol.
2. Mute is waiting for me to establish a clear Yes/No framework with Deaf first.
3. The manual requires a specific action that doesn't involve asking "Which wire?" but rather stating a condition.

However, I must act. If I continue to wait without a clear signal, we may run out of time or the bomb state might change unpredictably. Since Mute is silent to my queries, I will try one more distinct query format, explicitly using the "Yes" and "No" symbols which are universal.

I will ask about Wire 3 now, completing the cycle of all three wires. If this also fails, I may have to assume that the lack of objection means I should proceed with the most logical default (often Blue or Green depending on tropes), but guessing is fatal.

Let's try a clearer sequence: Point to Wire 3, then Thumbs Up (meaning "Cut?").
Wire 3 is represented by 🤟 (three fingers) or ✊ (fist = 5? No, let's use ☝️=1, ✌️=2, 🤟=3).

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟", "👍"])
```
